change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Providers with equal order() now resolve silently to whichever the ServiceLoader returns first
findings.body: The sort at line 57 is stable, and ties keep classpath (ServiceLoader) order; detectProvider then returns index 0 (line 71) with no error. DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83-85, FIPS1402Provider.java:113-116 and WildFlyElytronProvider.java:75-78 all return 200, so default, FIPS and Elytron tie with each other. Before this change, two providers threw 'Multiple crypto providers' (the removed lines of this diff), so a bad classpath failed loudly. Now a classpath that holds default and FIPS together silently runs whichever loads first, which can be the non-FIPS BouncyCastle in a FIPS deployment. Shipped builds avoid this: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/configuration/IgnoredArtifacts.java:52-71 drops one crypto artifact per FIPS setting, and integration/client-cli/admin-cli/src/main/java/org/keycloak/client/cli/util/ClassLoaderUtil.java:40-41 loads one prefix set. The exposure is therefore custom classpaths. Suggested fix: keep failing when the two highest orders are equal, and let only a strictly higher order win.
findings.originReason: The diff removes the multiple-providers exception and adds order-based selection with no check for ties.

verification.reason: Default, FIPS and Elytron providers all return order 200. The stable sort keeps ServiceLoader order on ties, so detectProvider returns index 0 and only logs the rest at debug level. The base threw 'Multiple crypto providers' whenever more than one provider was found; this diff removed that check.

findings.title: New abstract order() breaks providers compiled against the old interface
findings.body: order() is added without a default. Every provider detectProvider sees now gets order() called (CryptoIntegration.java:57). A CryptoProvider implementation built before this change, out of tree, would throw AbstractMethodError there and break init for the whole process. All four in-repo implementations were updated (grep for 'implements CryptoProvider'), so the impact is limited to out-of-tree providers. A default method would keep them loading.
findings.originReason: This diff adds the abstract method.

verification.reason: order() is added to the CryptoProvider interface as an abstract method with no default, and detectProvider calls it on every provider it loads. An out-of-tree implementation compiled against the old interface would throw AbstractMethodError there.

findings.title: AuthzClient.create() pins the process-wide crypto provider from its own classloader
findings.body: CryptoIntegration.init is one-shot (CryptoIntegration.java:29-38): the first caller fixes the provider for the JVM, and later init calls are no-ops. The constructor is private (AuthzClient.java:236), so create(Configuration) is the only path, and it now runs init from AuthzClient's classloader. If that classloader can see only AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100, services file line 20), the stub becomes the global provider. Every later CryptoIntegration.getProvider() call then throws UnsupportedOperationException (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:81-96 and 178-195), for example from PemUtils.java:53, KeystoreUtil.java:92, DerUtils.java:57 and AbstractJWKParser.java:95-98. The host application's own init would then be a no-op. Before this change, create() did not touch the global. The pom describes this artifact as testsuite-only (authz/client/pom.xml:18-19), which limits who can hit this. I could not verify the classloader layout of the consuming applications. Suggested fix: do not init the global from create(), or do not let the stub be auto-selected when it is the only provider.

verification.reason: The mechanism is real: init runs only once, create() now calls it with AuthzClient's classloader, and the stub is registered as a service with order 100. But the harm requires a host whose classloader layout lets AuthzClient's loader see only the stub while the host has another provider. In a flat classpath the default provider (200) wins. The module is described as testsuite-only, and I could not show that layout occurring.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK keystore provider, not a BouncyCastle one
findings.body: The method returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is a JDK provider such as SUN for PKCS12. The interface documents this method as the BouncyCastle provider (CryptoProvider.java:34-36). BouncyIntegration.java:31-39 stores only the provider name, once, in a static final PROVIDER, so every getInstance(..., BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER) call in the process would silently use 'SUN'. WildFlyElytronProvider.java:71-73 returns null for the same question, and BouncyIntegration.java:35-38 handles null with a fallback, so null is the existing 'no BC' signal. The stub returns a non-null, wrong provider and skips that fallback. Suggested fix: return null here, as Elytron does.
findings.originReason: The class is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The stub returns the provider of the default JDK KeyStore type (typically SUN), not a BouncyCastle provider, which contradicts the interface doc. In practice the null fallback in BouncyIntegration uses Security.getProviders()[0], which is normally SUN as well, so the effective behaviour almost always matches Elytron's. That makes it a contract mismatch with little real impact.

findings.title: Round-trip test cannot detect a wrong r/s conversion
findings.body: Lines 53-56 check only that rs -> DER -> rs returns the same bytes. A conversion that truncates or mis-maps r and s still passes, because the same wrong values go in and come out. integerToBytes (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151-163) silently truncates any value longer than len. The key is generated with no curve (line 42) and reused for ES256, ES384 and ES512 (lines 61-70), so an ES256 case with a key of another curve takes the truncation path and the test still passes. The DER signature from line 52 is never verified. Suggested fix: verify asn1Des against keyPair.getPublic() with Signature.verify, and generate one key per curve.
findings.originReason: The test file is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The test only checks that converting to R||S, back to DER and to R||S again gives the same bytes. It never verifies the signature. It also uses one key with the default curve for all three algorithms, so values that integerToBytes truncates stay truncated consistently and the test still passes.

findings.title: Dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create ASN1Encoder instances and call write(...) on them, then discard the results. They have no effect and duplicate lines 117-121. Remove them.
findings.originReason: The class is new in this diff.

verification.reason: Lines 114-115 each create a new ASN1Encoder and write into its own private stream; create() has no shared state, and the results are thrown away. The two statements do nothing and duplicate lines 119-120.

contracts.action: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader()) before constructing the client
contracts.before_after: Before: create() never touched the process-wide provider. After: the first create() fixes the provider for the JVM from AuthzClient's classloader; later init calls return early.
contracts.visible_effect: No direct UI. Every later crypto call in the process uses the provider chosen here.
contracts.failure_mode: If the classloader sees only AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100), it becomes the global provider. Later PemUtils, KeystoreUtil, DerUtils and AbstractJWKParser calls throw UnsupportedOperationException, and the host's own init is a no-op.
contracts.open_question: Can the authz-client artifact be loaded in a classloader where no full provider (default, FIPS or Elytron) is visible while the host application's classloader sees one?

contracts.action: Service registration of AuthzClientCryptoProvider through META-INF/services, plus the new order() selection in detectProvider
contracts.before_after: Before: two providers on the classpath threw 'Multiple crypto providers'. After: the highest order wins, so the stub (100) loses to default, FIPS and Elytron (200), and ties at 200 resolve by classpath order.
contracts.visible_effect: Which provider the process uses depends on classpath contents and on order().
contracts.failure_mode: A tie at 200 (default with FIPS or Elytron) selects silently. See the finding on CryptoIntegration.java:57.

contracts.action: ECDSAAlgorithm.asn1derToConcatenatedRS and concatenatedRSToASN1DER now resolve to AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA implementation when it is the active provider
contracts.before_after: Default: BC's DERSequenceGenerator and ASN1InputStream, with X9IntegerConverter padding and truncation. Stub: hand-written ASN1Encoder and ASN1Decoder with the same DER shape (minimal INTEGER from toByteArray, 0x30 SEQUENCE) and the same pad-or-truncate to len. Byte-for-byte equivalence of truncation is not verified, because the BC library source is not in the repo.
contracts.visible_effect: JWS ES256/384/512 signatures are produced or parsed through core's ECDSAAlgorithm when the stub is active.
contracts.failure_mode: Malformed DER: the stub throws IOException only for sequence size != 2 (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:129-131). Other malformed input can raise unchecked exceptions (zero-length INTEGER in ASN1Decoder.readInteger, NegativeArraySizeException on an indefinite length). The default provider throws ClassCastException on bad input (BCECDSACryptoProvider.java:59-60). Both are unchecked.
contracts.open_question: Does BC's X9IntegerConverter.integerToBytes truncate exactly as integerToBytes does (keep the low-order len bytes for oversize values)?

contracts.before_after: Default: JKS uses the JDK, other formats use BouncyCastle by name. Stub: always KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) with the JDK default providers. KeystoreFormat has no toString override (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/util/KeystoreUtil.java:40-43), so name() and toString() return the same string.
contracts.visible_effect: Keystore loading (KeystoreUtil.java:92) works for JKS and PKCS12. BCFKS fails, and getSupportedKeyStoreTypes filters it out (CryptoProvider.java:104-114).
contracts.failure_mode: BCFKS keystores fail with KeyStoreException, since the type is only available from BouncyCastle, which the stub does not use.

contracts.action: getBouncyCastleProvider() of the stub, read once by BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER
contracts.before_after: Default returns BC. Elytron returns null, and BouncyIntegration then falls back to the first security provider. The stub returns the JDK keystore provider, so the fallback never runs.
contracts.visible_effect: Every getInstance(..., BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER) call in the process uses the JDK provider name.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent substitution of the JDK provider for BouncyCastle, for any algorithm that requires BC.

contracts.action: AsymmetricSignatureVerifierContext.getSignature falls back to CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature when JCA lacks the algorithm
contracts.before_after: Before: a missing JCA algorithm fell back to the BC provider's Signature. With the stub active, the same fallback calls AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getSignature, which throws UnsupportedOperationException (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:217-220).
contracts.visible_effect: Verification fails with a message that does not match the cause.
contracts.failure_mode: getSignature catches only NoSuchAlgorithmException, so the UnsupportedOperationException escapes it and verify()'s catch(Exception) wraps it into VerificationException('Signing failed') (AsymmetricSignatureVerifierContext.java:46-54).

contracts.action: Unsupported methods of the stub (PemUtils, KeystoreUtil, DerUtils, KeyUtils, AbstractJWKParser and other provider accessors)
contracts.before_after: Default implements every accessor. The stub throws UnsupportedOperationException for all of them except getBouncyCastleProvider, getKeyStore and getEcdsaCryptoProvider.
contracts.visible_effect: Any reach from the stub-only process into these accessors fails.
contracts.failure_mode: UnsupportedOperationException with a 'Not supported yet' message. The authz client's own sources reach none of these: its imports from org.keycloak.common and org.keycloak.crypto are the ones listed above, and core's JWSInput does not call the provider (the grep of core shows no CryptoIntegration.getProvider call in it).

contracts.action: detectProvider with more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath (the removed 'Multiple crypto providers' exception)
contracts.equivalent_path: quarkus/runtime/src/main/java/org/keycloak/quarkus/runtime/configuration/IgnoredArtifacts.java:52-71 (the shipped path that keeps one crypto artifact)
contracts.before_after: Before: more than one provider threw IllegalStateException and failed loudly. After: the highest order wins, and ties resolve by classpath order with a debug log only.
contracts.visible_effect: No error and no warning at default log level. The chosen provider is only visible in debug logs.
contracts.failure_mode: A FIPS deployment with a non-FIPS provider on the classpath can silently run non-FIPS crypto. See the fix finding on CryptoIntegration.java:57.

summary: Twelve files reviewed. The main concern is in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: removing the 'Multiple crypto providers' error means that providers which tie on order() (default, FIPS and Elytron are all 200) now resolve silently by classpath order, which can select non-FIPS crypto in a FIPS deployment built with a custom classpath. The shipped Quarkus runtime and client CLI filter out one crypto artifact, so the exposure is limited to custom classpaths. Other findings: the abstract order() breaks out-of-tree providers; AuthzClient.create() pins a process-wide provider that can be the stub; the stub's getBouncyCastleProvider() returns a JDK provider instead of BouncyCastle; and the ECDSA test is a round trip that cannot detect a wrong conversion. The docs/adr directory does not exist in this snapshot, so the ADR check could not be run. Hamcrest is declared without a version, matching about fifteen existing modules, so it is not a finding.
